recipes.title: Aleppo Kibbeh
recipes.description: A bulgur torpedo pointed at both ends, filled with meat and pine nuts — the shell thin as paper.
instructions: Soak the bulgur 20 minutes in cold water and squeeze bone dry — any moisture left bursts the kibbeh in the oil.
Process the bulgur, 300 g of meat, flour and salt into a sticky, smooth paste. Chill 30 minutes.
Fry the onion, add the meat, baharat and pine nuts and cook 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Wet your hands, take a ball, and hollow it deep and very thin with a finger — in Aleppo a cook is judged on shell thickness.
Fill, seal, and point both ends into a torpedo.
Fry at 170°C for 6–7 minutes to a deep brown. Serve hot. Meat.

recipes.title: Kibbeh bi-Saniyeh
recipes.description: Two bulgur layers with filling between, baked in a tray and cut into diamonds.
instructions: Make the bulgur paste as for Aleppo kibbeh and divide in two.
Fry the onion, add the meat, baharat, pine nuts and pomegranate molasses and cook 10 minutes. Cool.
Oil a tin and press half the paste into a thin, even layer, keeping your hands wet throughout.
Spread the filling evenly.
Press the second half out on baking paper, invert it over the filling and seal the edges.
Score diamonds with a wet knife, drizzle olive oil and bake at 200°C for 45 minutes. Meat.

recipes.title: Kibbeh with Quince
recipes.description: Small kibbeh in a quince and pomegranate braise — a winter dish with no equivalent anywhere.
instructions: Make walnut-sized kibbeh with meat filling and fry them lightly until golden.
Peel the quinces and cut thick slices. Drop them straight into lemon water — quince browns within minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic, add the quince and sugar and cook 10 minutes.
Add water and pomegranate molasses and cook 25 minutes until the quince softens but holds its shape.
Add the fried kibbeh and cook another 25 minutes without stirring.
Scatter dried mint in the last two minutes. Meat.

recipes.title: Kibbeh Mabrouma
recipes.description: A long bulgur roll coiled into a spiral in the tin — hard to make, and impossible to hide a shortcut in.
instructions: Make the bulgur paste and chill 30 minutes — cold, it stretches without tearing.
Fry the onion, add the meat, walnuts, baharat and pomegranate molasses and cook 10 minutes. Cool.
Roll the paste between two sheets of baking paper into a long thin strip 12 cm wide.
Lay the filling along one edge and roll into a thin log using the paper.
Coil the log into a spiral in an oiled round tin, from the centre outwards.
Drizzle olive oil and bake at 200°C for 40–45 minutes until golden. Meat.

recipes.title: Lahm bi-Ajine
recipes.description: Thin dough rounds under a film of meat, pomegranate molasses and Aleppo pepper — small and sour.
instructions: Froth the yeast and water 10 minutes, add flour, oil and salt and knead 8 minutes. Rise 1 hour.
Mix the meat, well-squeezed onion, grated tomato, pomegranate molasses and Aleppo pepper.
Drain the mixture in a sieve for 20 minutes. Wet topping will not cling to the dough and burns in the oven.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll thin 10 cm rounds.
Spread a very thin film of meat right to the edge.
Bake at 250°C for 8–10 minutes only, on a preheated tray. Meat.

recipes.title: Burghul bi-Dfeen
recipes.description: Coarse bulgur, chickpeas and meat in one pot — the home food you make when there are no guests.
instructions: Sear the lamb in olive oil, add the onion and fry 12 minutes.
Add the soaked chickpeas, baharat, cinnamon and water and cook an hour until the chickpeas soften.
Rinse the coarse bulgur once only — repeated rinsing strips starch that is needed to bind.
Add the bulgur to the pot and stir through.
Cook covered 25 minutes at the lowest heat, without stirring.
Off the heat, cover with a towel and rest 15 minutes before serving. Meat.

recipes.title: Potato Kibbeh
recipes.description: The parve version — potato and bulgur filled with walnuts, pine nuts and raisins.
instructions: Soak the bulgur 20 minutes and squeeze.
Mash the potatoes hot and mix with the bulgur, salt and baharat into an even paste.
Fry the onion in olive oil 15 minutes to a deep brown — that is all the flavour here, since there is no meat.
Add the walnuts, pine nuts, raisins and pomegranate molasses and cook 5 minutes. Cool.
Press half the paste into a tin, spread the filling, and cover with a second layer.
Score diamonds, drizzle olive oil and bake at 200°C for 35 minutes. Parve.

recipes.title: Lentil Kibbeh
recipes.description: A lentil and bulgur shell with onion and sesame — a fasting dish that became a dish in its own right.
instructions: Cook the lentils in water 20 minutes until fully collapsed.
Add the bulgur to the hot lentil water, take off the heat and cover 15 minutes — the bulgur takes it all up.
Mash to an even paste and correct the salt and cumin.
Fry the onion in olive oil 18 minutes to a deep sweet brown. Set half aside.
Mix the remaining half with toasted sesame and sumac.
Press half the paste out, spread the filling, cover, score and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes. Parve.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Kibbeh
recipes.description: An orange, sweet shell around walnut and chickpea — a colour nothing else on the plate competes with.
instructions: Roast the pumpkin at 200°C for 40 minutes and mash. Drain it in a sieve for 20 minutes — watery pumpkin will not hold a shell.
Soak the bulgur 20 minutes, squeeze, and mix with the drained pumpkin and salt.
Fry the onion, add roughly crushed chickpeas, walnuts, pomegranate molasses and sumac and cook 6 minutes.
Press half the pumpkin paste into an oiled tin.
Spread the filling and cover with a second layer.
Score, drizzle olive oil and bake at 200°C for 35 minutes. Parve.

recipes.title: Bulgur with Tomato
recipes.description: Coarse bulgur with tomato and fried onion — twenty minutes, and no meat at all.
instructions: Fry the onion in olive oil 12 minutes to a deep brown.
Add the tomato paste and Aleppo pepper and fry 3 minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the grated tomato and cook 8 minutes.
Add the bulgur and stir a minute until every grain is coated.
Add boiling water and salt, cover and cook 15 minutes at the lowest heat.
Off the heat, scatter dried mint and rest 10 minutes covered. Parve.

recipes.title: Yebra — Stuffed Vine Leaves
recipes.description: Rolls as thin as a finger filled with rice and meat, in a pot with lemon and pomegranate.
instructions: Blanch the vine leaves 2 minutes and drop into cold water.
Mix uncooked rice, meat, olive oil, baharat and salt.
Put a teaspoon at the base of each leaf, fold the sides and roll as thin as a finger — a thick yebra is considered coarse work.
Line a pot with torn leaves and tomato slices and pack the rolls in tight layers.
Tuck whole garlic cloves between the layers and pour in water, lemon and pomegranate molasses to cover.
Set a heavy plate on top and cook 80 minutes over low heat. Dried mint at the end. Meat.

recipes.title: Yalanji — Vine Leaves in Oil
recipes.description: "The fake" — the same leaves without meat, filled with rice, pine nuts and raisins, and served cold.
instructions: The name means "the fake" — it imitates yebra without meat, and it is a separate dish rather than a lesser one.
Blanch the leaves 2 minutes and cool.
Fry the onion in olive oil 15 minutes to a deep brown — here the onion takes the meat's place.
Add rice, pine nuts, raisins, pomegranate molasses and salt and stir 3 minutes.
Roll thin, pack into a lined pot, and pour in water, lemon and olive oil to cover.
Cook 50 minutes and cool in the pot. Served cold. Parve.

recipes.title: Stuffed Courgettes
recipes.description: Hollowed courgettes filled with rice and meat in a tomato and mint braise — without yogurt.
instructions: Hollow the courgettes with a corer, leaving a 3–4 mm wall. Any thinner and they tear as they cook.
Mix uncooked rice, meat, baharat, salt and a little olive oil.
Fill two thirds only — the rice swells.
Lay the courgettes flat in a wide pot, in one or two layers.
Pour over the grated tomato, garlic, water and lemon to two thirds of the height.
Cook 60 minutes over low heat and scatter dried mint at the end. The traditional version is simmered in yogurt; this one is tomato. Meat.

recipes.title: Sheikh el-Mahshi
recipes.description: "The sheikh of stuffed things" — small aubergines filled with meat and pine nuts only, with no rice at all.
instructions: Deep-fry the whole aubergines until soft and drain on a rack.
Slit each one lengthwise and open it gently like a boat.
Fry the onion, add the meat, baharat and pine nuts and cook 10 minutes. No rice — that is what earns it the name.
Fill each aubergine generously and pack them into a tin touching one another.
Mix the grated tomato, pomegranate molasses and water and pour around them, not over the filling.
Bake covered at 190°C for 40 minutes, then uncovered for 15. Meat.

recipes.title: Stuffed Peppers
recipes.description: Red peppers filled with rice and meat in a pomegranate and Aleppo-pepper braise.
instructions: Cut the tops off the peppers and clear the seeds. Keep the lids.
Fry the onion, add the meat, baharat and Aleppo pepper and cook 6 minutes, then mix with uncooked rice.
Fill two thirds and close with the lids.
Stand the peppers upright and tightly packed in a pot — that is what stops the filling spilling.
Pour in the grated tomato, pomegranate molasses and water to half their height.
Cook covered 60 minutes over low heat. Meat.

recipes.title: Stuffed Potatoes
recipes.description: Hollowed, fried potatoes filled with meat in a thick tomato braise.
instructions: Peel and hollow the potatoes with a corer, leaving a half-centimetre wall.
Deep-fry the hollow shells for 3 minutes only — they need to set, not to cook through.
Fry the onion, add the meat, baharat and pine nuts and cook 8 minutes.
Fill each potato and pack it down firmly.
Stand them in a tin and pour the grated tomato, paste and water to half their height.
Bake at 190°C for 50 minutes until completely tender. Meat.

recipes.title: Stuffed Onions
recipes.description: Whole onion layers wrapped around meat — the stuffed dish that asks for the most patience.
instructions: Cut a vertical slit in each onion right to the centre and blanch 12 minutes.
Separate the layers carefully. The innermost ones are too small — keep them for another pot.
Mix uncooked rice, meat, baharat and salt.
Put a spoonful in each layer and roll into a tight cylinder.
Pack into a pot lined with the onion offcuts and pour in water, pomegranate molasses, tamarind and sugar.
Set a plate on top and cook 70 minutes over low heat. Dried mint at the end. Meat.

recipes.title: Sour Stuffed Aubergines
recipes.description: Small aubergines in a lemon and garlic braise — sharply sour, with no tomato at all.
instructions: Hollow the small aubergines, leaving a thin wall.
Mix uncooked rice, meat, baharat, salt and olive oil and fill two thirds.
Pack into a pot and scatter whole garlic cloves between them.
Pour in water and lemon juice to cover — there is no tomato here, and the lemon is all the liquid.
Set a plate on top and cook 60 minutes over low heat.
Scatter dried mint at the end. Served hot or at room temperature. Meat.

recipes.title: Stuffed Chard Leaves
recipes.description: Green leaves around rice, lentils and herbs — parve, and lighter than the vine leaves.
instructions: Blanch the chard leaves for 10 seconds only — they are far more delicate than vine leaves and collapse fast.
Strip the thick rib from each leaf with a knife.
Fry the onion in olive oil 15 minutes to a deep brown.
Mix with uncooked rice, cooked lentils, herbs, sumac and salt.
Roll and pack tightly into a lined pot.
Pour in water, lemon and olive oil and cook 45 minutes. Served at room temperature. Parve.

recipes.title: Ijjeh — Herb Omelette
recipes.description: A green omelette with more herb than egg — fried in small patties and served cold.
instructions: Chop the herbs very fine — ijjeh is mostly greens, and the egg only holds them together.
Beat the eggs with the flour, Aleppo pepper, salt and pepper.
Fold in all the herbs and spring onion. The mixture should look almost entirely green.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls in and fry 3 minutes a side until the edges crisp.
Drain and serve at room temperature with lemon. Parve.

recipes.title: Kebab Karaz — Cherry Kebab
recipes.description: Small lamb meatballs in sour cherry sauce — the dish Aleppo is known for wherever it is known at all.
instructions: Knead the lamb with baharat, salt and pepper for 4 minutes and chill 30.
Roll hazelnut-sized meatballs — small, because they finish cooking inside the sauce.
Sear them in olive oil until browned all over and lift out.
Pit the cherries and cook them with the sugar for 25 minutes until they collapse into a thick sauce.
Add the pomegranate molasses and correct — the sauce should be mainly sour, with the sweetness only balancing.
Return the meatballs and cook 20 minutes. Serve on pita with pine nuts. Meat.

recipes.title: Aleppo Kebab
recipes.description: Skewered kebab with Aleppo pepper and parsley — gently hot rather than burning.
instructions: Squeeze the grated onion bone dry — wet onion drops the kebab off the skewer.
Knead the meat with everything for 5 minutes — kneading develops the protein that holds it on the skewer.
Chill an hour, covered.
Wet your hands and press the meat along flat skewers with your fingers.
Grill over glowing coals 4 minutes a side, turning once only.
Grill tomatoes and onions alongside and serve in pita. Meat.

recipes.title: Riz bi-Hamud
recipes.description: Chicken and root vegetables in a sharp lemon broth over white rice — Aleppo's comfort food.
instructions: Boil the chicken and skim until the broth runs clear.
Cook 45 minutes, lift the chicken out and pull it into pieces.
Add the potato, carrot and kohlrabi to the broth and cook 20 minutes.
Fry the crushed garlic in olive oil for 30 seconds only and stir it in — this is the taqliya, and it is what gives the smell.
Return the chicken, add the lemon juice and cook 10 minutes.
Scatter dried mint and serve over white rice. Meat.

recipes.title: Chicken in Pomegranate Molasses
recipes.description: Chicken roasted under a dark pomegranate glaze with walnuts — sour, glossy and nearly black.
instructions: Mix the pomegranate molasses, honey, garlic, Aleppo pepper, olive oil and salt into a marinade.
Rub the chicken pieces and chill at least 3 hours — the molasses needs time to go in.
Spread sliced onion across a tin and set the chicken on it.
Bake covered at 190°C for 50 minutes.
Uncover, baste from the pan juices every 10 minutes, and bake another 25.
Scatter toasted walnuts. The glaze will be very dark — that is right, not burnt. Meat.

recipes.title: Kebab with Aubergine
recipes.description: Lamb patties and fried aubergine alternating in a tin, in tomato and pomegranate sauce.
instructions: Salt the aubergine slices 30 minutes, squeeze and fry until golden. Drain.
Knead the lamb with the squeezed onion, Aleppo pepper, baharat and salt, and shape flat patties.
Sear the patties in a pan 2 minutes a side.
Arrange in a tin alternating: aubergine, patty, tomato slice, and repeat, standing on the diagonal.
Mix the tomato paste, pomegranate molasses and water and pour over.
Bake at 190°C for 40 minutes. Meat.

recipes.title: Freekeh with Chicken
recipes.description: Smoked green wheat with chicken, almonds and cinnamon — a smokiness that comes from the grain, not the fire.
instructions: Rinse the freekeh three times and drain — it is a roasted grain and carries a lot of burnt residue.
Simmer the chicken in water with a whole onion, cinnamon and allspice for 45 minutes. Strain and keep the broth.
Pull the chicken into large pieces.
Fry the chopped onion in olive oil 10 minutes, add the freekeh and stir 3 minutes.
Add the boiling stock and cook covered 30 minutes over low heat.
Lay the chicken over, scatter toasted nuts and rest 10 minutes covered. Meat.

recipes.title: Kefta in Tahini
recipes.description: Lamb patties baked under a tahini and lemon sauce — tahini is parve, so this is a meat dish and not a mixed one.
instructions: Knead the lamb with the squeezed onion, parsley, baharat and salt and press into a tin in an even layer.
Lay potato slices over and roast at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Whisk the raw tahini with cold water gradually — it seizes and then loosens; that is normal.
Add lemon, garlic and salt to a sauce the thickness of cream.
Tahini is parve — so this sauce over meat is not a mixture, unlike a yogurt sauce would be.
Pour the tahini over and bake another 25 minutes. Scatter pine nuts. Meat.

recipes.title: Arayes
recipes.description: Pita filled with a thin layer of meat and grilled until crisp, the fat soaking inward.
instructions: Mix the lamb, squeezed onion, parsley, pomegranate molasses, Aleppo pepper, salt and pepper.
Halve each pita and open it into a pocket.
Spread a very thin layer of meat inside — too thick and the bread burns before the meat cooks.
Brush the outside with olive oil.
Grill or cook in a cast-iron pan 5 minutes a side, pressing with a spatula.
The fat soaks into the bread and crisps it. Cut into triangles. Meat.

recipes.title: Samak Harra — Spicy Fish
recipes.description: A whole fish baked under a blanket of coriander, garlic and walnut — the Syrian coast's dish.
instructions: Clean the fish and cut diagonal slashes on both sides. Salt and leave 20 minutes.
Blend the coriander, garlic, walnuts and Aleppo pepper with the olive oil into a thick green paste.
Brush half the paste over the fish and into the slashes.
Bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
Mix the remaining paste with the tahini and lemon into a sauce.
Pour it over the fish and return for 10 minutes. Parve — served hot or cold.

recipes.title: Sayadieh — Fish on Onion Rice
recipes.description: Fish over rice the colour of caramel from deeply fried onion — the colour is the onion, not a spice.
instructions: Fry the onion in olive oil for 25 minutes to a very dark brown, nearly burnt. That is the whole source of colour and flavour.
Set a third of the onion aside for the top.
Add water to the onion pot, simmer 10 minutes and strain — this gives a brown stock.
Cook the rice in the brown stock with the cumin, 25 minutes covered.
Salt the fish, fry 3 minutes a side and set aside.
Lay the fish on the rice, scatter the reserved onion and almonds, and serve with tahini and lemon. Parve.

recipes.title: Muhammara
recipes.description: Roasted red peppers, walnuts and pomegranate molasses — the dip Aleppo gave the world.
instructions: Char the peppers over flame or in a 250°C oven until the skin blackens through.
Cover in a bowl 15 minutes, peel and seed. Drain them 20 minutes — wet pepper makes watery muhammara.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan 5 minutes and cool.
Pulse the walnuts, peppers, garlic, crumbs and spices in short bursts — smooth muhammara is not muhammara.
Add the pomegranate molasses and olive oil and pulse 10 seconds more.
Rest 2 hours refrigerated before serving. Parve.

recipes.title: Makdous — Oil-Cured Stuffed Aubergines
recipes.description: Tiny aubergines filled with walnut and garlic, kept for months under olive oil.
instructions: Trim the stems and blanch the aubergines 8 minutes — until a knife goes in but they are not soft.
Slit each one and salt generously inside. Set them cut side down on a tilted surface for 12 hours to drain fully.
The draining is the whole thing: one drop of water left will grow mould in the jar within a week.
Mix the walnuts, garlic, Aleppo pepper and salt and pack into each aubergine.
Layer into a sterilised jar with the chillies between them.
Pour olive oil to cover completely, and check again after two days. Ready in two weeks. Parve.

recipes.title: Mutabbal
recipes.description: Charred aubergine with tahini and lemon, smooth and creamy — with nothing in it that hides the smoke.
instructions: Char the aubergines over open flame 20 minutes until the skin blackens and the flesh collapses.
Peel and drain in a sieve for 40 minutes. That time is the difference between mutabbal and water.
Mash with a fork, not a processor. A processor turns it into grey foam.
Add the tahini, lemon, garlic and salt and mix by hand.
Taste and balance: the tahini should support the smoke, not cover it.
Drizzle olive oil and scatter pomegranate and mint. Parve.

recipes.title: Aleppo Tabbouleh
recipes.description: A parsley salad with only a little bulgur — the greens are the dish and the grain is merely present.
instructions: Soak the bulgur in the lemon juice alone, not water, for 20 minutes. It takes up the acid and softens.
Wash the parsley and dry it completely. A wet leaf turns the salad to mush.
Chop the parsley very fine with a sharp knife. A processor bruises the leaf and releases water.
Chop the mint, spring onion and tomato equally fine.
Combine everything with the soaked bulgur, olive oil and sumac.
Salt only just before serving — salt draws water out of the tomatoes. Parve.

recipes.title: Fattoush
recipes.description: A vegetable salad with toasted pita and sumac — the bread goes in last, always.
instructions: Tear the pitas by hand and toast at 200°C for 8 minutes until fully crisp.
Cut the vegetables into coarse chunks — fattoush is a coarse salad, unlike tabbouleh.
Chop the herbs roughly and add.
Whisk the pomegranate molasses, olive oil, lemon, sumac and salt into a dressing.
Pour over the vegetables and toss.
Add the bread only at serving. Pita that sits in dressing stops being fattoush. Parve.

recipes.title: Tomato Salad with Pomegranate Molasses
recipes.description: Ripe tomatoes, onion and pomegranate molasses — three ingredients doing all the work.
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into thick wedges, not dice — a wedge keeps its juice inside.
Salt the red onion, leave 10 minutes, then rinse and squeeze.
Whisk the pomegranate molasses, olive oil, sumac and salt into a dressing.
Lay the tomatoes on a flat plate and scatter the onion.
Pour the dressing over without tossing — tossing turns this into pulp.
Scatter torn mint and Aleppo pepper. Parve.

recipes.title: Aleppo Za'atar
recipes.description: A za'atar blend with pistachio — what tells the Aleppo one apart from every other.
instructions: Toast the sesame in a dry pan 4 minutes until golden, shaking constantly.
Toast the pistachios and walnuts separately for 3 minutes — they burn sooner.
Cool everything completely before mixing.
Grind the pistachios and walnuts coarsely in a mortar, not to a powder. The pieces are what identify Aleppo za'atar.
Mix with the ground za'atar, sumac, cumin and salt.
Keep sealed up to two months. Served with olive oil and bread. Parve.

recipes.title: Lemon-Cured Olives
recipes.description: Cracked green olives in brine with lemon and Aleppo pepper — three weeks and done.
instructions: Crack each olive with a light tap of a rolling pin — do not cut. A crack opens the olive to the salt without breaking it apart.
Soak in cold water for five days, changing the water daily. That draws out the bitterness; without it they cannot be eaten.
Make the brine: 1 cup salt to 3 litres water, boiled. Cool completely.
Layer the olives, lemon slices, garlic and peppers into a jar.
Pour the brine to cover and add a layer of olive oil on top — the oil blocks the air.
Seal and wait 3 weeks. Scatter Aleppo pepper before serving. Parve.

recipes.title: Labneh
recipes.description: Yogurt drained for a day until it spreads like cheese — the base of every breakfast.
instructions: Stir the salt through the yogurt — the salt is what draws the liquid out, not just seasoning.
Line a sieve with doubled cheesecloth and pour the yogurt in.
Tie the cloth into a bundle and hang it over a bowl in the fridge.
Drain 12 hours for soft labneh, 24 hours for labneh firm enough to roll into balls.
Turn into a bowl and stir until smooth.
Drizzle olive oil and scatter za'atar and mint. A dairy dish.

recipes.title: Shanklish
recipes.description: Aged cheese rolled in za'atar, crumbled with tomato and onion — very sharp.
instructions: Crumble the shanklish by hand into coarse lumps, not crumbs. The lump is part of the eating.
Chop the tomato and onion very fine and drain off excess liquid.
Salt the onion, leave 10 minutes, then squeeze — shanklish is sharp enough without raw onion.
Fold gently through the cheese without mashing it.
Add the olive oil and lemon juice.
Scatter za'atar and torn mint and serve with bread. A dairy dish.

recipes.title: Date Ma'amoul
recipes.description: Semolina domes filled with date, stamped in a carved wooden mould — on oil, so they can follow meat.
instructions: Rub the coarse and fine semolina together with the oil by hand. Rest overnight, covered — the semolina has to drink the oil and there is no shortcut.
Next day add the water, rose water and blossom water and knead only lightly.
Work the date paste with a spoon of oil and roll small balls.
Take a ball of dough, hollow it, fill with date and seal.
Stamp in a carved wooden mould and knock it out against the table.
Bake at 170°C for 22–25 minutes — they must stay pale. Dust with icing sugar once cool. Parve.

recipes.title: Pistachio Ma'amoul
recipes.description: The same dough, filled with pistachio and orange blossom — green inside and white out.
instructions: Make the semolina dough as for the date ma'amoul, including the overnight rest.
Grind the pistachios fairly coarse — too fine a powder disappears in the mouth.
Mix with the sugar and blossom water into a damp filling that holds when pressed.
Fill each ball of dough and stamp in a different mould from the date ones — that is how you tell the filling without breaking one.
Bake at 170°C for 22 minutes, keeping them pale.
Cool completely before dusting — warm, they absorb the sugar. Parve.

recipes.title: Karabij Halab with Natef
recipes.description: Semolina and walnut cookies served in a white natef foam — whipped from soapwort root, and so entirely parve.
instructions: Make the semolina dough and walnut filling, shape elongated fingers and bake at 170°C for 22 minutes.
The natef is the dish: boil the crushed soapwort root in 3 cups of water for 45 minutes until reduced to one cup.
Strain well. The brown liquid whips like egg white — that is a property of the root, not of any egg.
Cook the sugar and water into a thick syrup and cool slightly.
Whip the soapwort liquid 10 minutes and pour the syrup in a thin stream while whipping, to a stiff white foam.
Add the rose water. Serve the karabij standing in the natef. Completely parve — no egg and no dairy.

recipes.title: Barazek
recipes.description: Thin cookies with sesame on one side and pistachio on the other — two textures in one biscuit.
instructions: Knead the flour, oil, icing sugar, water and rose water into a soft dough. Chill 30 minutes.
Mix the sesame with the honey and a little water into a sticky mass.
Scatter the chopped pistachios on baking paper in small flat heaps.
Roll small balls of dough, dip one side in the sesame and press the other onto a pistachio heap.
Set them pistachio side down and flatten very thin.
Bake at 175°C for 18–20 minutes until the sesame golds. Parve.

recipes.title: Ka'ak el-Eid
recipes.description: Savoury-sweet rings with sesame and mahlab — eaten with coffee rather than as dessert.
instructions: Froth the yeast, sugar and water 10 minutes.
Add flour, oil, mahlab, fennel and salt and knead 8 minutes. Rise 1 hour.
Roll finger-thick ropes and join into 8 cm rings.
Dip each ring in water and then in sesame on both sides — the water is the glue.
Prove on the tray 25 minutes.
Bake at 190°C for 22–25 minutes until golden. Parve — they keep two weeks sealed.

recipes.title: Bitter Orange Preserve
recipes.description: Rolls of bitter orange peel tied with thread and cooked in syrup — bitterness turned into sweetness.
instructions: Lightly grate off the outermost layer of peel — it is too bitter to leave on.
Peel wide strips, roll each into a tight cylinder and tie with kitchen thread.
Soak three days in cold water, changing it twice a day. That step decides whether the preserve is bitter or not.
Boil 20 minutes and drain.
Cook the sugar, water and cloves into a syrup, add the rolls and cook 90 minutes at the lowest heat.
Add the lemon juice for the last 10 minutes. The peel turns translucent. Parve.

recipes.title: Balouza
recipes.description: A half-translucent cornflour and rose-water pudding — a parve dessert that looks like a dairy one.
instructions: Mix the cornflour with one cup of cold water until there are no lumps at all.
Boil the remaining three cups with the sugar.
Pour the cornflour mixture in slowly while whisking constantly.
Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy and no longer tasting of starch.
Off the heat, add the rose water and blossom water.
Pour into glasses and chill 4 hours. Scatter pistachios and pomegranate. Parve — as sweet as a milk pudding, with no milk.

recipes.title: Jallab
recipes.description: A cold drink of date syrup and rose water, with pine nuts and raisins floating on top.
instructions: Soak the pine nuts in cold water for 30 minutes — they soften and float rather than sink.
Soak the raisins 15 minutes and drain.
Mix the jallab syrup with the cold water and rose water.
Taste and adjust — jallab should be sweet but not thick; it is a drink, not a dessert.
Fill glasses with crushed ice and pour.
Scatter the pine nuts and raisins on top. They will float. Parve.

recipes.title: Halawet el-Jibn
recipes.description: Rolls of melted cheese dough filled with clotted cream — pink, soft and served cold in syrup.
instructions: Boil the water and sugar and add the semolina in a thin stream, stirring, for 3 minutes.
Add the cheese and stir over the lowest heat until it melts into a smooth, stretchy mass, about 8 minutes.
Turn onto baking paper brushed with rose water and press into a thin sheet while hot — cold, it no longer stretches.
Cut into strips the width of a palm.
Lay ashta along each strip and roll up.
Drizzle syrup, scatter pistachios and chill an hour. A dairy dish — cheese and cream together.

recipes.title: Mamounia
recipes.description: A buttered semolina porridge served hot for breakfast — Aleppo's oldest sweet.
instructions: Boil the water and sugar into a light syrup and keep it hot.
Melt the butter in a heavy pot and add the semolina.
Toast the semolina 10–12 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden-brown and smelling nutty. That step sets the flavour.
Pour the hot syrup in carefully — it will boil up and spit.
Stir 5 minutes until thick and pulling from the sides.
Add the rose water and serve hot with white cheese and cinnamon. Dairy.
